When I try and run lavInspect() exactly as written in the error, I get:

Error in lavListInspect(object = object, what = what, add.labels = add.labels,  : 
  unknown `what' argument in inspect function: `optim.gradient'

I've tried running lavInspect(fit, "optim") as well and gotten the same error. Also get the same errors when trying with lavListInspect(). Not sure where to go from here!

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: lavInspect Error
parts:
lavInspect(fitaswrittenGHControl, "optim.gradient")

Error in lavListInspect(object = object, what = what, add.labels = add.labels,  : 
  unknown `what' argument in inspect function: `optim.gradient'

The clue is in the error message referring to lavListInspect().  This option is not available for lavaan.mi objects (which inherit from lavaanList objects) because the optimizer doesn't have one solution, it has one solution per data set. 

I think the problem might be resolved if you change the argument fun='lavaan' to fun='cfa' so that the appropriate default identification constraints are chosen, which are not specified in your syntax.  lavaan() is a bare-bones function that does not assume much beyond what your syntax explicitly specifies, whereas cfa() and sem() make some reasonable guesses such as freely estimating residual variances (except for ordinal items).  Given that your latent y* scales are fixed to 1 (default delta parameterization), your model-implied residual variances should be less than 1.  I don't think your models are identified, but would be using the cfa() defaults.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen
